limitations: Produced in a host session and accepted by the CP-OS check.
Literal checked analytical handoff, not native contract acceptance; source qualifications and gaps remain.

- No filing states an EBITDA or an adjusted EBITDA, so EBITDA (Reported) is derived for every period as operating income plus depreciation and amortization, and no adjusted figure or bridge to one is stated; this restricts comparison of leverage and cover with any issuer or agency measure. Severity medium. The action that would close it is the issuer's own adjusted EBITDA reconciliation, if it publishes one; until then the derived measure stays labelled. - The cash flow statements print year-to-date amounts only, so discrete Q2 and Q3 depreciation and amortization, and with it discrete Q2 and Q3 EBITDA for 2025 and 2026, are derived by subtraction, and no discrete Q2 or Q3 cash flow is stated. Severity low. The derived quarters stay labelled as derived. - No balance sheet is printed at 2025-03-31, 2025-06-30 or 2025-09-30 and no fourth-quarter 2025 statements are printed, so net debt and leverage at those dates and a discrete fourth quarter are not stated and the last-twelve-months series starts at 2026-03-31. Severity medium. Nothing in the five filings closes it; a fourth quarter can be derived by subtraction and labelled. - The only debt maturity table and lease maturity table are at 2025-12-31, so the maturity ladder and the principal reconciliation are drawn there and no maturity profile is stated at 2026-09-30; the other debt of USD 8.3 million has no stated obligor, rate, maturity or security. Severity medium. A later maturity table, if published, would close it. - The 2030 row of the 2025-12-31 maturity table is a dash. The row is left out of the debt maturities table rather than written as zero, and the printed principal total of USD 713.3 million equals the rows listed. Severity low. - Finance leases of USD 35.6 million and other debt of USD 8.3 million are left out of the debt stack because no source states their legal rank, and the finance leases' security is not stated. Severity low. The lease and loan documents would close it. - The ABL borrowing base is not printed, and reported availability of USD 89.1 million at 2026-09-30 is USD 29.4 million below the commitment net of letters of credit; undrawn committed facilities in the liquidity table is the reported availability. Severity medium. A borrowing base certificate would close it. - FY2025 cash interest paid of USD 23.3 million is not a run rate because the first coupon on the 2031 senior secured notes was paid in January 2026, so FY2025 cover of 7.45x flatters; the 2026 rows use last-twelve-months cash interest. Severity medium. FY2025 cover should be read with that limit. - The 2023-12-31 balance sheet column is on the FY2024 report's presentation: capitalized contract costs are printed as outsourcing assets of USD 31.6 million against USD 35.3 million in the FY2025 report, and prepaid and other long-term assets at 2023-12-31 are not re-presented. Totals, debt and cash are unaffected. Severity low. - Dashes printed in the filings are recorded as not supplied and never as zero: goodwill impairment for FY2023, Q2 2025, H1 2025 and Q3 2026, loss before income taxes for Q2 2025, debt extinguishment, gain on sale of properties, sale proceeds, issuance costs and foreign exchange forward lines in several columns, and inventories for FY2023. Lines a report does not print, such as the impairment line in the Q1 reports, are recorded as not printed. Severity low. - No guarantor financial information is printed for the three subsidiary guarantors, so the share of earnings, debt and cash at the guarantors is not established and structural subordination is described in text only. Severity medium. Summarized guarantor financial information, if it exists, would close it. - Cash taxes paid for FY2024 and FY2023 are the amounts disclosed before the 2025 disclosure change, with no breakdown by jurisdiction. Severity low. - The Brazil payment after the balance-sheet date is dated only to the fourth quarter of 2026 and its amount is approximate, so the pro forma net debt and net leverage are approximate and other fourth-quarter cash flows are not reflected. Severity medium. The fourth-quarter report would close it. - The pension settlement events of 2025 and 2026 print a settlement loss, an amount of obligations transferred and a smaller amount reclassified out of accumulated other comprehensive loss, and the filings do not reconcile them; none of the three is in EBITDA. Severity low.

facts.text: The view would change in three ways. A large holder, or insider representation on the board, would turn the pension-led policy into a question of owner conduct. facts.label: Company and business model
facts.text: Unisys is an IT services company whose volume comes from labour-based managed services and whose profit comes disproportionately from one proprietary software franchise. Services were 82.61% of FY2025 revenue of USD 1,950.1 million, spread across digital workplace (26.07%), cloud, applications and infrastructure (37.58%) and enterprise computing (32.25%), and the enterprise computing segment sells ClearPath licences and support to an installed base concentrated in financial services, travel and transportation and healthcare. facts.label: Revenue drivers and pricing power
facts.text: Revenue is predictable at contract level but structurally flat to declining, and pricing power is limited outside ClearPath. Nine-month total contract value rose 21.93% and new business rose 61%, but technology solutions and services renewals fell 5%, and the company states that competitors offer more aggressive pricing and that AI has reduced and replaced some historical services, leading clients to delay spending. The mechanism is that services renewals face price pressure from competitors and from automation savings that clients capture, while ClearPath licence revenue is recognised in full when a term begins, so quarterly revenue swings with renewal timing; the implication is that revenue visibility supports cash flow only if renewals are won at stable prices, and ClearPath renewal contract value, up 33% over nine months, is the offsetting support. facts.text: Margins are hard to defend under volume pressure because overhead absorbs most of gross profit and cost cuts need cash first. Gross margin was 28.17% in FY2025 and 25.73% in the nine months of 2026, and selling, general and administrative expense took 79.34% of nine-month gross profit, so a small revenue shortfall moves earnings sharply. facts.text: EBITDA does not convert into free cash flow available for debt service. facts.label: Competitive forces
facts.text: Rivalry is the force that matters most to credit: the company names systems integrators, consultants, outsourcers and hardware and software providers as competitors, some with greater resources and more aggressive pricing, and digital workplace gross margin fell from 15.86% to 11.17% between the first nine months of 2025 and 2026, which links rivalry directly to earnings. Substitutes are a second force, because AI and automation have reduced and replaced some historical services and an accelerated shift of ClearPath to subscription would delay cash receipts. Buyers are large enterprises and governments with budget power, softened by the absence of any client above 10% of revenue; new entrants are less of a threat to the ClearPath installed base because of switching costs, and suppliers matter through scarce skilled labour and a limited set of component suppliers. facts.label: Strengths, weaknesses, opportunities and threats in credit terms
facts.text: Strengths are the absence of any maturity before 2031, a high-margin installed-base franchise, contract backlog and a diversified client list, and the absence of owner-driven leakage. Weaknesses are fixed claims that absorb 94.23% of EBITDA, a digital workplace business with falling profit, earnings that depend on one fourth-quarter renewal season, and a pension obligation that competes for cash. Opportunities that could improve credit quality are the completion of the pension settlement programme in the first half of 2027, which should reduce required contributions, growth in ClearPath renewals and managed services for AI workloads, and cost savings from restructuring. Threats that could weaken it are AI-driven substitution of services, competitor pricing, a shift of ClearPath to subscription, and a single refinancing window in 2030 and 2031 at a time when the pension schedule is still heavy. facts.label: Financial profile and credit quality
facts.text: Across nine dimensions the profile is mostly average with weakness where cash is concerned. Scale and market position are average: revenue of USD 1,957.1 million over the last twelve months is modest against competitors that the company says have greater resources. Competitive advantage is average, strong in the ClearPath installed base and weak in digital workplace. Business diversification is average, with three segments, no client above 10% and 47.59% of FY2025 revenue earned outside the United States and the United Kingdom, but profit is concentrated. Cost and capex flexibility is average, since capital expenditure is 4.33% of revenue but overhead absorbs 79.34% of gross profit. Margin stability is weak, with EBITDA margin of 8.91% in FY2025 and 9.28% on the last twelve months, down from 10.15% in FY2024. Free cash flow stability is weak, with an outflow of USD 46.4 million. Ability to refinance and access capital markets is average, shown by the June 2025 refinancing but at a higher coupon and with ratings of B and B2. Liquidity position is average, with USD 353.3 million and no maturity before 2031. Financial policy and governance are average, with no sponsor, unqualified audit opinions and a debt-funded pension contribution. The main supports are the maturity profile and the ClearPath franchise; the main constraints are cash conversion and the pension; the trend is stable revenue with weaker cash, and the missing datapoints are covenant levels, the borrowing base and an issuer-defined EBITDA. facts.label: Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds
facts.text: Over the next 12 to 24 months earnings depend on the fourth-quarter 2026 renewal season, while cash depends on interest and pensions: the coupon is fixed at about USD 74.21 million a year and pension contributions are about USD 97 million in 2026 and about USD 101 million in 2027, so the cash gap stays negative on last-twelve-months earnings and liquidity funds it. Tailwinds are rising contract value, backlog above the prior year, an improving cloud segment margin of 22.48%, a joint venture margin benefit of about USD 12 million in 2026 and cost actions; headwinds are the ClearPath nine-month decline, falling digital workplace profit, AI substitution, competitor pricing and the loss of the joint venture benefit if the transaction does not recur. Over three to five years the pension settlement programme should lower obligations, contributions of about USD 241 million over 2028 to 2030 are lighter than 2026, and the decisive event is refinancing the ABL in June 2030 and the notes in January 2031, which is easier if EBITDA has recovered. Management gives no numeric revenue or earnings guidance in the filings, so this outlook is the analyst's reading of the disclosed schedules. facts.label: Downside scenario
facts.text: The scenario that matters is a further decline in ClearPath renewals and digital workplace profit, not a generic recession. The first operational break would be a weak fourth-quarter renewal season, because enterprise computing supplied an implied 74.75% of fourth-quarter 2025 segment gross profit. If the observed nine-month declines were repeated, with ClearPath revenue down 9.14% at the enterprise computing gross margin and digital workplace gross profit down 28.05%, EBITDA would fall by about USD 42.46 million to USD 139.24 million, total leverage would rise to 5.25x, cover would fall to 1.68x and the fixed-claims cash gap would widen to USD 116.77 million a year. Liquidity of USD 353.3 million would then last about 3.03 years, shorter than the 4.16 years to the notes' maturity, and a smaller receivables base would also reduce ABL availability and move it toward the USD 12.5 million level at which the fixed charge test applies. Management levers are capital expenditure, restructuring and the pension settlement schedule, but none of them closes a gap of that size without damaging the ClearPath and services base; resilience appears sufficient to avoid a liquidity crisis for about three years but not to refinance the notes from internal cash, and the ratio of the stress to the cushion is an illustration, not a forecast. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_uis-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 72–73; calculation C8; calculation C10; calculation C13; calculation C17

facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, Unisys presents an adequate business profile supported by an installed-base software franchise, contract backlog and the absence of any maturity before 2031, but credit quality is constrained by fixed claims that absorb 94.23% of EBITDA (74.31% before a non-cash impairment), falling digital workplace profit and a heavy pension schedule. Cash-flow durability appears weak because free cash flow was an outflow of USD 46.4 million. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on EBITDA recovering before the 2030 and 2031 window, and on the fourth-quarter renewal season in between. The primary downside path is a weak ClearPath renewal season combined with continued digital workplace erosion, which raises leverage to 5.25x and uses liquidity before the notes mature. Further analysis would require the issuer's own EBITDA definition, covenant levels, the borrowing base, the US share of future pension contributions and the proxy statement. Top risk: fixed interest and pension claims that exceed earnings in a business whose profit depends on a single renewal season. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C6; calculation C7; calculation C17

spans.text: # CP-0 Source readiness for Unisys Corp (uis-746838), as of 2026-11-18
## Request

Unisys Corp (issuer uis-746838), as of 2026-11-18, pathway credit_snapshot: source readiness for the Business & governance, Financial foundation and Fundamental credit modules. Scope is the five supplied SEC filings (Forms 10-K for FY2024 and FY2025; Forms 10-Q for Q1, Q2 and Q3 2026), with no legal documents, ratings, quotes, peers or portfolio supplied. This module assesses source readiness only and gives no credit view.

Document date is the signature date. |
No earlier module output is supplied to this module.
## Findings
### Bottom line

The five Unisys filings are sufficient for a filings-only financial, business and fundamental credit review through 30 September 2026, but covenant, governance and issuer-defined EBITDA conclusions stay provisional because the documents that hold them are absent. The statements, debt notes, revolving-facility terms, pension funding and segment results needed for those modules are printed for FY2025 and each quarter of 2026, and the latest filing was signed 13 days before the 2026-11-18 cutoff. A discrete fourth quarter of 2025 and a maturity schedule at 30 September 2026 are not printed, so those inputs must be derived or taken from earlier dates.

No credit agreement or indenture is supplied, so the level of the springing fixed-charge covenant, the company's reported ratio and the headroom are not established. The 2026 proxy statement that carries board, pay and ownership data is absent, and no filing states an adjusted EBITDA, so any leverage multiple would be an analyst construction. The gate therefore passes for the three requested modules with these limits attached.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Leverage has risen from 2.42x total debt to EBITDA at FY2024 to 4.03x on a last-twelve-months basis at 2026-09-30 (net 2.57x, 2.61x pro forma for a USD 7 million Brazil payment in the fourth quarter of 2026), so creditors depend on earnings recovery. The filings state no EBITDA, so the measure is operating income plus depreciation and amortization: USD 181.7 million over the last twelve months after USD 48.7 million of impairment, and USD 230.4 million before it. Cash interest paid was USD 82.9 million over the same period, so cover is 2.19x; the 7.45x for FY2025 flatters because the first coupon on the 2031 senior secured notes fell in 2026.

Basis: calculation C21; calculation C22; calculation C46; calculation C49; 10-Q_2026-09-30_uis-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_uis-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-K_2025-12-31_uis-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 121

Total debt rose by USD 248.5 million in FY2025 to USD 741.7 million, and cash fell by USD 149.7 million between 2025-12-31 and 2026-09-30. Liquidity inputs total USD 353.3 million against debt of USD 731.4 million.
Basis: calculation C52; calculation C53; calculation C55; 10-Q_2026-09-30_uis-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_uis-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20
### Leverage and coverage

Gross leverage rose because debt rose while earnings fell. Total debt went from USD 493.2 million at FY2024 to USD 741.7 million at FY2025 when the June 2025 offering of the 2031 senior secured notes replaced the 2027 notes and also funded part of the US pension deficit, while derived EBITDA fell from USD 203.8 million to USD 173.7 million. The creditor consequence is that the same earnings now carry USD 248.5 million more debt at a higher coupon, and the interest line already shows it: interest expense was USD 53.4 million in FY2025 against USD 31.9 million in FY2024.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_uis-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 91–92; 10-K_2025-12-31_uis-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 70; calculation C52; calculation C3; calculation C2

The strongest contrary evidence is that last-twelve-months EBITDA of USD 181.7 million carries a non-cash impairment of USD 48.7 million; before it, leverage is 3.17x total and 2.03x net, and that view wins if no further impairment follows and earnings hold at the pre-impairment level. What would change the view the other way is a further year of cash interest at the current USD 82.9 million with no EBITDA recovery, because cover is already 2.19x on a last-twelve-months basis and only 1.17x after capital expenditure.
Basis: calculation C50; calculation C22; calculation C63; 10-Q_2026-06-30_uis-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 4
### Cash flow quality

Operating cash flow is negative because pension contributions absorb it: net cash from operating activities was an outflow of USD 140.0 million in FY2025 after pension and postretirement contributions of USD 345.3 million, USD 250 million of them a discretionary pension contribution, and an outflow of USD 66.5 million in the nine months of 2026 after USD 89.0 million of contributions. Free cash flow after marketable software and capital additions was an outflow of USD 46.4 million over the last twelve months, so debt service and pension funding both draw on cash rather than on cash generation.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_uis-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 92–93; 10-K_2025-12-31_uis-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 73; 10-Q_2026-09-30_uis-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5–6; calculation C31

Working capital is a second drain: accounts payable and current liabilities used USD 79.3 million in the nine months of 2026, and deferred revenue, a non-debt funding float that clients prepay, fell from USD 329.2 million at 2025-12-31 to USD 253.6 million at 2026-09-30. The mechanism is that the float funded operations and its decline of USD 75.6 million is cash that must now come from the balance sheet; the implication is that a shrinking float adds to the cash drain from interest and pension funding.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_uis-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5–6; calculation C51; 10-K_2025-12-31_uis-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 91–92
### Liquidity and maturities

Liquidity inputs are USD 264.2 million of cash (excluding USD 12.3 million of restricted cash) and USD 89.1 million of ABL availability, and the Brazil payment would lower cash by about USD 7 million, so pro forma cash is not established. Of the cash, USD 187.1 million is held abroad and about one-quarter of that may not be readily transferable. The ABL matures in June 2030, so no committed facility expires within twelve months, and availability is limited by a receivables borrowing base that the filings do not print: it is USD 29.4 million below the commitment net of letters of credit.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_uis-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_uis-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_uis-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37; calculation C55

The maturity wall is a single bullet: at 2025-12-31 the only principal after FY2029 is the USD 700.0 million of 2031 senior secured notes, against USD 13.3 million of other debt falling due from FY2026 to FY2029. The consequence is that refinancing risk sits in January 2031 and in the ABL springing maturity, which brings the ABL forward to 91 days before any date on which US pension contributions above USD 100.0 million are required unless liquidity above USD 130.0 million and other conditions are met.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_uis-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 121; 10-K_2025-12-31_uis-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 72; calculation C44
### Definitions, data quality and conflicts

Every ratio here rests on a derived EBITDA, which is the main definition risk: the filings state none, so operating income plus the four depreciation and amortization lines is used without add-backs, and the issuer's own adjusted measure, if one exists, is not supplied. Interest is the second: the nine-month interest on the 2031 notes of USD 57.7 million exceeds the interest expense line of USD 55.8 million by USD 1.9 million, and FY2025 cash interest of USD 23.3 million omits the first coupon on the 2031 notes, so cover for FY2025 is not a run rate. The 2024-12-31 balance sheet and the 2023-12-31 capitalized contract costs were printed differently in the two annual reports, and the later report is used for 2024.
### Subsequent events and multi-figure items

One event after the balance-sheet date changes net debt: the 2026-09-30 report states that a Brazil tax reserve of about USD 7 million was paid in the fourth quarter of 2026, which raises net debt to USD 474.2 million and net leverage to 2.61x on the same EBITDA, and it is kept out of the period figures. The September 2026 pension annuity is a multi-figure event: about USD 200 million of obligations transferred, a pre-tax settlement loss of USD 151.2 million and USD 121.4 million reclassified out of accumulated other comprehensive loss, none of which enters EBITDA because the loss sits below operating income.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_uis-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-09-30_uis-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_uis-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23; calculation C46

## Gaps

- No filing states an EBITDA or an adjusted EBITDA, so EBITDA (Reported) is derived for every period as operating income plus depreciation and amortization, and no adjusted figure or bridge to one is stated; this restricts comparison of leverage and cover with any issuer or agency measure. Severity medium. The action that would close it is the issuer's own adjusted EBITDA reconciliation, if it publishes one; until then the derived measure stays labelled.

- The cash flow statements print year-to-date amounts only, so discrete Q2 and Q3 depreciation and amortization, and with it discrete Q2 and Q3 EBITDA for 2025 and 2026, are derived by subtraction, and no discrete Q2 or Q3 cash flow is stated. Severity low. The derived quarters stay labelled as derived.

- No balance sheet is printed at 2025-03-31, 2025-06-30 or 2025-09-30 and no fourth-quarter 2025 statements are printed, so net debt and leverage at those dates and a discrete fourth quarter are not stated and the last-twelve-months series starts at 2026-03-31. Severity medium. Nothing in the five filings closes it; a fourth quarter can be derived by subtraction and labelled.

- The only debt maturity table and lease maturity table are at 2025-12-31, so the maturity ladder and the principal reconciliation are drawn there and no maturity profile is stated at 2026-09-30; the other debt of USD 8.3 million has no stated obligor, rate, maturity or security. Severity medium. A later maturity table, if published, would close it.

- The 2030 row of the 2025-12-31 maturity table is a dash. The row is left out of the debt maturities table rather than written as zero, and the printed principal total of USD 713.3 million equals the rows listed. Severity low.

- Finance leases of USD 35.6 million and other debt of USD 8.3 million are left out of the debt stack because no source states their legal rank, and the finance leases' security is not stated. Severity low. The lease and loan documents would close it.

- The ABL borrowing base is not printed, and reported availability of USD 89.1 million at 2026-09-30 is USD 29.4 million below the commitment net of letters of credit; undrawn committed facilities in the liquidity table is the reported availability. Severity medium. A borrowing base certificate would close it.

- FY2025 cash interest paid of USD 23.3 million is not a run rate because the first coupon on the 2031 senior secured notes was paid in January 2026, so FY2025 cover of 7.45x flatters; the 2026 rows use last-twelve-months cash interest. Severity medium. FY2025 cover should be read with that limit.

- The 2023-12-31 balance sheet column is on the FY2024 report's presentation: capitalized contract costs are printed as outsourcing assets of USD 31.6 million against USD 35.3 million in the FY2025 report, and prepaid and other long-term assets at 2023-12-31 are not re-presented. Totals, debt and cash are unaffected. Severity low.

- Dashes printed in the filings are recorded as not supplied and never as zero: goodwill impairment for FY2023, Q2 2025, H1 2025 and Q3 2026, loss before income taxes for Q2 2025, debt extinguishment, gain on sale of properties, sale proceeds, issuance costs and foreign exchange forward lines in several columns, and inventories for FY2023. Lines a report does not print, such as the impairment line in the Q1 reports, are recorded as not printed. Severity low.

- No guarantor financial information is printed for the three subsidiary guarantors, so the share of earnings, debt and cash at the guarantors is not established and structural subordination is described in text only. Severity medium. Summarized guarantor financial information, if it exists, would close it.
- Cash taxes paid for FY2024 and FY2023 are the amounts disclosed before the 2025 disclosure change, with no breakdown by jurisdiction. Severity low.

- The Brazil payment after the balance-sheet date is dated only to the fourth quarter of 2026 and its amount is approximate, so the pro forma net debt and net leverage are approximate and other fourth-quarter cash flows are not reflected. Severity medium. The fourth-quarter report would close it.

- The pension settlement events of 2025 and 2026 print a settlement loss, an amount of obligations transferred and a smaller amount reclassified out of accumulated other comprehensive loss, and the filings do not reconcile them; none of the three is in EBITDA. Severity low.

spans.text: # CP-1A Business & governance for Unisys Corp (uis-746838), as of 2026-11-18
## Request

Unisys Corp (issuer uis-746838), as of 2026-11-18, pathway credit_snapshot: the business, transaction, ownership, governance and operating-model facts that matter to creditors. Scope is the five supplied SEC filings (Forms 10-K for FY2024 and FY2025; Forms 10-Q for Q1, Q2 and Q3 2026) and the source readiness answer, in US dollars in millions unless stated. No sponsor document, proxy statement, credit agreement or indenture is supplied, and no credit recommendation is given.
## Sources
| Source | Document | Document date | sha256 | Use |

Document date is the signature date. |

Document date is the signature date. |

| 10-Q_2026-09-30_uis-20260930.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended 30 September 2026 | 2026-11-05 | b4db927423314831657abfb4a4e8e47de8ad829f8e833f971ecb4627a2ea5a41 | Latest source: segments, clients and backlog at 2026-09-30, shares outstanding, the September 2026 pension annuity, the Brazil tax settlement, the goodwill write-off and the subsequent payment. Document date is the signature date. |
| Module | Code | sha256 | Use |

| Source readiness | CP-0 | e2fb1cba1f3c97c383f13e1245d8285e099d3975153d78efcc3298259a11ac10 | Source inventory and the gaps already logged for the five filings; the absence of a proxy statement, indenture and credit agreement |
## Findings
### Bottom line

Unisys has no identified controlling shareholder or financial sponsor, so creditor risk lies in its own financial policy and a narrow earnings base, not in owner extraction, and its 2025 choice to borrow secured debt partly for pensions makes that base matter more. The June 2025 refinancing raised debt principal by USD 215.0 million and annual cash coupon by about USD 41.03 million, and about USD 200 million of the proceeds funded a USD 250 million discretionary pension contribution.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_uis-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 70–74; 10-K_2024-12-31_uis-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 113; calculation C13; calculation C14; calculation C12

Profit sits in one place. The enterprise computing segment, built on the ClearPath software franchise, earns 61.17% of segment gross profit on 33.63% of segment revenue, while the digital workplace segment earns a 14.54% gross margin and has had all of its goodwill written off. The filings show no dividend since 1990 and no share repurchases in 2025, so owner extraction is not in evidence.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_uis-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 143; 10-Q_2026-09-30_uis-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-K_2025-12-31_uis-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 60; calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C3
### Key findings

- Ownership gives creditors no sponsor to assess and no fee, distribution or recapitalisation pattern to price. The stock is listed in New York, held by a few thousand stockholders of record, and the aggregate market value held by non-affiliates was USD 300.4 million at 2025-06-30, small against debt of USD 741.7 million at 2025-12-31. The equity cushion is thin and there is no owner with a stated willingness or capacity to support the notes.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_uis-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 1–2; 10-K_2025-12-31_uis-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 60; Source readiness (CP-0)

- Financial policy has been mixed and pension-led. The 2025 refinancing moved the maturity from 2027 to 2031 but at a higher coupon and a larger secured principal, and 80.00% of the 2025 discretionary pension contribution was borrowed. Annuity purchases in each year from 2023 to 2026 cut pension obligations at non-cash settlement losses of USD 857.2 million in total, and a further settlement is expected in 2027. Creditors gain a smaller pension claim, but at the price of a heavier secured debt stack.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_uis-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 70–74; 10-K_2024-12-31_uis-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 54; 10-Q_2026-09-30_uis-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_uis-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 39; calculation C12; calculation C15

- Earnings depend on the ClearPath franchise, whose revenue is lumpy rather than clearly weakening. ClearPath revenue fell 9.14% in the nine months to 2026-09-30 but rose 1.7% in the third quarter, and renewal contract value rose 33% over the nine months. The enterprise computing segment's share of segment gross profit held at 53.10% against 53.34% a year earlier; the 61.17% for FY2025 is higher because enterprise computing supplied an implied 74.75% of fourth-quarter segment gross profit. The filing says seasonality has not generally moved quarterly revenue materially, yet implied fourth-quarter 2025 revenue was 24.84% above the third quarter, so earnings and cash hinge on the fourth-quarter renewal season.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_uis-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-Q_2026-09-30_uis-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_uis-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 30; 10-Q_2026-09-30_uis-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 36; 10-K_2025-12-31_uis-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-K_2025-12-31_uis-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 143; calculation C3; calculation C7; calculation C8; calculation C21; calculation C23

- The digital workplace segment is low-margin and its profit is falling, and its goodwill is gone. Revenue rose 2.17% in the nine months to 2026-09-30, but gross profit fell 28.05% and the gross margin was 11.17% against 15.86% a year earlier, after 14.54% for FY2025. Cumulative goodwill impairments reached USD 141.3 million with the second quarter 2026 charge, so no goodwill remains to impair, but weak segment profit leaves less to absorb cost-reduction cash.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_uis-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 143; 10-Q_2026-09-30_uis-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_uis-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 25; calculation C2; calculation C7; calculation C16; calculation C22

- Revenue visibility is reasonable and client concentration is low. Backlog was USD 3.16 billion at 2025-12-31 and 35.13% of it was expected to convert in 2026, no client exceeded 10% of revenue, and revenue was broadly stable in the nine months to 2026-09-30 after a 2.90% decline in FY2025. Visibility is contract-based, not a commitment, and public-sector and sector concentrations inside enterprise computing remain.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_uis-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-K_2025-12-31_uis-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 19–20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_uis-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37; calculation C4; calculation C8; calculation C10

- Governance disclosure is adequate for monitoring but incomplete for control. The audit committee is wholly independent, the auditor gave unqualified opinions on the statements and on internal control, and the company states it met all covenants. Board composition, related-party dealings, director independence and holder percentages sit in a proxy statement that is not supplied, and earlier control weaknesses in 2022 were remediated in 2023.
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against the view that owner behaviour is not a creditor risk is what the filings do not show: holder percentages, board seats, related-party dealings and director independence are all in a proxy statement that is not supplied, so a large holder or activist could exist without appearing here. Equity awards are also sizeable, with outstanding restricted stock and units equal to 9.07% of shares, which aligns employees with shareholders more than creditors. The strongest evidence against concern about the earnings base is stabilisation: nine-month revenue up 0.51%, backlog of USD 2.92 billion at 2026-09-30 above USD 2.83 billion a year earlier, third-quarter ClearPath revenue up 1.7% and nine-month ClearPath renewal contract value up 33%.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_uis-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 145; 10-K_2025-12-31_uis-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 130; 10-Q_2026-09-30_uis-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_uis-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 30; 10-Q_2026-09-30_uis-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 36; 10-Q_2026-09-30_uis-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37; calculation C8; calculation C10; calculation C17

The view would change in three ways. A large holder, or insider representation on the board, would turn the pension-led policy into a question of owner conduct. An indenture or credit agreement that permits large restricted payments would make the absence of distributions a choice rather than a limit. A fall in ClearPath revenue through the fourth-quarter renewal season, or the planned 2027 pension settlement funded with new debt, would move the assessment from mixed to adverse, while a strong renewal season would support the stabilisation case.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_uis-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 30; 10-Q_2026-09-30_uis-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 39; 10-K_2025-12-31_uis-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 70–71; calculation C8; calculation C21
### Limitations

- The proxy statement is not among the sources, so the conclusion that no controlling shareholder, sponsor or activist exists rests on the cover page, the stockholder count and the absence of any sponsor in the notes; a large holder would reverse it.

- No indenture or credit agreement is supplied, so what the documents let the company pay out, borrow or secure is not established, and the view that financial policy has been mixed rests on actions taken, not on capacity.

- Segments are reported only to gross profit, so the concentration of profit in the enterprise computing segment is a gross profit finding and not an operating profit one; allocated overhead could narrow or widen it.
- The 2024 and 2023 segment figures were re-presented after the January 2025 reorganisation, so segment trends before FY2025 rest on the later report's figures and not on the earlier report's.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

The one new debt issue in the five filings is the June 2025 refinancing. The company sold USD 700.0 million of secured notes due 2031 in a private placement, used them with cash to buy back USD 480.1 million of its secured notes due 2027 and discharge the remaining USD 4.9 million, and put about USD 200 million toward a discretionary pension contribution. It also extended its asset-based revolver, with USD 125.0 million of commitments, from October 2027 to June 2030.

- No proxy statement is supplied, so beneficial ownership percentages, board composition, director independence and related-party dealings are not established; the conclusion that no controlling shareholder or activist exists rests on the cover page and the stockholder count. - No indenture or credit agreement is supplied, so capacity to pay dividends, borrow, grant liens, move assets or amend terms is not established, and the fixed charge coverage level and the company's ratio are not printed. Severity high. The indenture dated 2025-06-27 and the Amended and Restated Credit Agreement would close it.

- The current Chair of the Board is not stated in the FY2025 report, which says only that a new chief executive has been in role since April 2025; the FY2024 report had said the former chief executive would remain Chair. Severity low. The proxy statement would close it.

- Segments are reported to gross profit only, so the concentration of profit in enterprise computing is measured before allocated overhead. Severity medium. A segment operating profit disclosure would close it.

- The nature of the first-quarter 2026 United Kingdom joint venture transaction is not described, so whether the margin benefit of about USD 12 million recurs is not established. Severity low. Later filings would close it.

- The terms of the consent amendments made to the 2027 notes in the June 2025 tender and the identity of tendering holders are not stated, so equal treatment of holders is not tested. Severity low. The tender offer documents would close it.

- Segment revenue for FY2024 and FY2023 is printed on two structures; the re-presented figures of the FY2025 report are used for every comparison. Severity low. The original figures are kept in the conflict log.

- The size of the September 2025 annuity purchase is stated as about USD 316 million and about USD 320 million in different reports, and the year of the March 2024 settlement loss is mislabelled in one sentence of the FY2025 report; both are kept as stated. Severity low.

- The no-dividend statement dates from the FY2025 report and the 2026 interim reports are silent on dividends, although each lists no unregistered sales or repurchases of equity; an event between 2026-11-05 and 2026-11-18 would not appear in any supplied source. Severity low.

- No discrete fourth-quarter 2025 statements are printed, so fourth-quarter revenue and enterprise computing gross profit are derived by subtracting the nine-month figures in the interim report from the full-year figures in the annual report; the seasonal pattern rests on that subtraction. Severity low. A fourth-quarter 2025 release would close it.

- The terms of the change of control agreement filed for each executive officer in the third quarter of 2026 are not summarised in the report, so the cost of a change of control to the company is not sized. Severity low. The exhibit itself would close it.

- The Brazil tax settlement payment is dated only to the fourth quarter of 2026 and its amount is approximate, so cash after 2026-09-30 is not fully reflected. Severity low. The fourth-quarter report would close it.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Unisys is a fragile credit that is liquid for now: nothing matures before January 2031 and liquidity is USD 353.3 million, but interest, pension funding and capital spending exceed earnings, so creditors rely on the ClearPath renewal season. Leverage is 4.03x total and 2.57x net on last-twelve-months EBITDA of USD 181.7 million (2.61x net pro forma for the Brazil payment in the fourth quarter of 2026), and cover is 2.19x.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_uis-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_uis-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C4

The coupon on the 2031 notes and 2026 pension contributions absorb 94.23% of that EBITDA, or 74.31% before a non-cash impairment, ahead of capital spending. Profit is concentrated in the enterprise computing segment, which earned 61.17% of FY2025 segment gross profit, while digital workplace gross margin fell to 11.17%. A strong fourth-quarter renewal season would improve the view and a further ClearPath decline would weaken it.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_uis-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 39; calculation C5; calculation C6; calculation C13; calculation C14
### Key findings

- Liquidity and the maturity profile are the main supports, but the cushion is finite. The only debt maturing before 2031 totals USD 13.3 million, the ABL runs to June 2030, and liquidity of USD 353.3 million would fund the fixed-claims cash gap of USD 74.31 million a year for about 4.75 years, against 4.16 years to the 2031 notes' maturity. That cash is also what the company would need to refinance the notes, so the runway does not remove refinancing risk.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_uis-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 72; 10-K_2025-12-31_uis-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 70; calculation C4; calculation C7; calculation C8

- Earnings do not cover fixed claims comfortably. Cover is 2.19x on last-twelve-months cash interest and 1.17x after capital expenditure, and free cash flow was an outflow of USD 46.4 million because the coupon and 2026 pension contributions take 94.23% of EBITDA. Before the USD 48.7 million non-cash impairment, EBITDA would be USD 230.4 million, the share 74.31% and total leverage 3.17x, so the weakness is in cash conversion more than in reported earnings.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C6; calculation C7

- The pension is the swing factor in cash flow and in liquidity access. Contributions were USD 343.7 million in FY2025, are about USD 97 million in 2026 and about USD 101 million in 2027, and total about USD 241 million over 2028 to 2030. The ABL matures early if US contributions above USD 100.0 million are required unless liquidity conditions are met; US contributions are about USD 47 million for 2026, so the trigger is distant this year, but the US share of later years is not established.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_uis-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 40; 10-Q_2026-09-30_uis-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 39; 10-K_2025-12-31_uis-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 72; calculation C9

- Profit depends on the ClearPath franchise, which is lumpy rather than clearly weakening, while digital workplace is the weak link. Enterprise computing earned 61.17% of FY2025 segment gross profit and an implied 74.75% of fourth-quarter 2025 segment gross profit; ClearPath revenue fell 9.14% in the nine months to 2026-09-30 but renewal contract value rose 33%. Digital workplace gross margin was 11.17% in those nine months against 15.86% a year earlier, and its goodwill is fully written off.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_uis-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-Q_2026-09-30_uis-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 36; calculation C13; calculation C14

- Financial policy is mixed rather than aggressive, and no owner is in evidence either to extract value or to provide support. No dividend has been paid since 1990 and no shares were repurchased, but 80.00% of the 2025 discretionary pension contribution was funded with the new secured notes, and board composition and holder percentages are not established.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_uis-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 60; 10-K_2025-12-31_uis-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 73; calculation C16

- Refinancing capacity is adequate today but concentrated in one window. The ABL matures in June 2030 and the notes in January 2031, about 7 months apart, with the notes redeemable at par from 2030-01-15; the agencies rated the company B and B2 with stable outlooks at the 2025 annual report, and the 2025 refinancing priced 3.75 percentage points above the coupon it replaced. A recovery in EBITDA before 2030 is the condition for refinancing at a lower cost.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_uis-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 70–72; 10-K_2025-12-31_uis-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 40; calculation C8; calculation C16
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a fragile view is that the cash gap rests partly on a non-cash impairment and on a pension schedule that eases: before the impairment, EBITDA is USD 230.4 million, leverage is 3.17x total and 2.03x net, and the gap narrows to USD 25.61 million, while contributions average about USD 80.33 million a year over 2028 to 2030 against about USD 97 million in 2026. Demand indicators are also improving, with backlog of USD 2.92 billion at 2026-09-30 above USD 2.83 billion a year earlier, nine-month total contract value up 21.93% and third-quarter revenue up 2.46%.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_uis-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-Q_2026-09-30_uis-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 36; 10-Q_2026-09-30_uis-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 25; calculation C3; calculation C7; calculation C9; calculation C15

The view would improve if the fourth-quarter renewal season lifted last-twelve-months EBITDA toward the pre-impairment USD 230.4 million, which would bring total leverage to 3.17x and the cash gap to USD 25.61 million. It would weaken if the nine-month declines in ClearPath revenue and digital workplace gross profit were repeated, which would cut EBITDA by about USD 42.46 million to USD 139.24 million, lift total leverage to 5.25x and use up liquidity in about 3.03 years, before the 2031 maturity. A US pension contribution requirement above USD 100.0 million, or ABL availability falling toward the USD 12.5 million test level, would also change the view.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_uis-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 72; 10-K_2025-12-31_uis-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 73; calculation C3; calculation C7; calculation C10; calculation C17
### Limitations

- No filing states an adjusted or covenant EBITDA, so every leverage and cover multiple here is built from operating income and depreciation and amortization; on the company's own definition each could be higher or lower, and the conclusion that cash cover is thin rests on that choice.

- The ABL borrowing base and fixed charge coverage level are not printed, and pension estimates for 2027 onward are global rather than the US-only measure that triggers the ABL springing maturity, so how close liquidity is to a facility trigger is not established and could shorten the runway.

- No discrete fourth-quarter statements, peer set, agency commentary or market prices are supplied, so the dependence on the renewal season rests on subtraction of nine-month figures and sector standing and market access rest on the filings alone.
- The downside scenario applies observed nine-month rates to a gross margin proxy, so its EBITDA, leverage and runway figures show direction and scale, not a forecast.
### Company and business model

Unisys is an IT services company whose volume comes from labour-based managed services and whose profit comes disproportionately from one proprietary software franchise. Services were 82.61% of FY2025 revenue of USD 1,950.1 million, spread across digital workplace (26.07%), cloud, applications and infrastructure (37.58%) and enterprise computing (32.25%), and the enterprise computing segment sells ClearPath licences and support to an installed base concentrated in financial services, travel and transportation and healthcare. Multi-year contracts and licence renewals give cash-flow visibility, with backlog of USD 3.16 billion at 2025-12-31, and no client exceeds 10% of revenue; the cost is that services are exposed to price competition, so debt-service capacity depends on holding the ClearPath base while services margins recover.

### Ownership and group structure

Unisys is publicly held with no controlling shareholder or financial sponsor identified, so no owner is positioned to extract cash or to supply equity if liquidity tightens, and the equity cushion is thin: the total deficit was USD 408.3 million at 2026-09-30 and the market value held by non-affiliates was USD 300.4 million at 2025-06-30. Debt sits at the parent with three wholly owned US guarantors; liabilities of other subsidiaries, including pension plans and trade payables, rank ahead of the notes in those subsidiaries, and the 51% owned United Kingdom joint venture shares its profit with three financial institutions. Federal loss carryforwards of USD 1.82 billion carry a full valuation allowance and an ownership change would limit them. Directors, independence and related-party dealings sit in a proxy statement that is not supplied, so governance beyond an independent audit committee is not established.

### Revenue drivers and pricing power

Revenue is predictable at contract level but structurally flat to declining, and pricing power is limited outside ClearPath. Nine-month total contract value rose 21.93% and new business rose 61%, but technology solutions and services renewals fell 5%, and the company states that competitors offer more aggressive pricing and that AI has reduced and replaced some historical services, leading clients to delay spending. The mechanism is that services renewals face price pressure from competitors and from automation savings that clients capture, while ClearPath licence revenue is recognised in full when a term begins, so quarterly revenue swings with renewal timing; the implication is that revenue visibility supports cash flow only if renewals are won at stable prices, and ClearPath renewal contract value, up 33% over nine months, is the offsetting support. Revenue fell 2.90% in FY2025 and rose 0.51% in the nine months of 2026, with currency adding 2 percentage points to third-quarter growth.
### Cost structure and margin resilience

Margins are hard to defend under volume pressure because overhead absorbs most of gross profit and cost cuts need cash first. Gross margin was 28.17% in FY2025 and 25.73% in the nine months of 2026, and selling, general and administrative expense took 79.34% of nine-month gross profit, so a small revenue shortfall moves earnings sharply. Digital workplace cost of revenue rose 7.87% in the nine months against revenue growth of 2.17%, which shows adverse operating leverage in the weakest segment, and the workforce is labour-based with 28.00% of staff in India, which lowers cost but adds currency exposure. Net cost-reduction charges were USD 30.5 million in FY2025 and the remaining workforce liability was USD 14.1 million at 2026-09-30, so savings are a lever but they are paid for up front and are not quantified in the filings.

### Capital intensity and cash conversion

EBITDA does not convert into free cash flow available for debt service. Capital expenditure and capitalised software absorbed USD 84.8 million over the last twelve months, 4.33% of revenue, which leaves EBITDA less capital expenditure of USD 96.9 million against cash interest of USD 82.9 million; after pension contributions, cash taxes and working capital, free cash flow was an outflow of USD 46.4 million. A fall in deferred revenue of USD 75.6 million since 2025-12-31 removed a non-debt funding float that clients had prepaid, which adds to the drain, and finance leases of USD 35.6 million are inside debt while operating leases are outside it. Capital expenditure is partly discretionary and is the main internal lever, but cutting it would also cut the software that supports the ClearPath renewals.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_uis-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-Q_2026-09-30_uis-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18; calculation C2; calculation C11
### Competitive forces

Rivalry is the force that matters most to credit: the company names systems integrators, consultants, outsourcers and hardware and software providers as competitors, some with greater resources and more aggressive pricing, and digital workplace gross margin fell from 15.86% to 11.17% between the first nine months of 2025 and 2026, which links rivalry directly to earnings. Substitutes are a second force, because AI and automation have reduced and replaced some historical services and an accelerated shift of ClearPath to subscription would delay cash receipts. Buyers are large enterprises and governments with budget power, softened by the absence of any client above 10% of revenue; new entrants are less of a threat to the ClearPath installed base because of switching costs, and suppliers matter through scarce skilled labour and a limited set of component suppliers.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_uis-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 36–38; 10-K_2025-12-31_uis-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-K_2025-12-31_uis-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 18; calculation C14
### Macro, regulatory and technology factors

Three categories change credit outcomes. Public-sector budgets and political decisions can reduce, delay or terminate government contracts, and the company reports that this has hurt results before; currency matters because 59.34% of FY2025 revenue was earned outside the United States and about one quarter of the USD 187.1 million of foreign cash may not be readily transferable; and interest rates and discount rates drive the pension contributions that compete with debt service. Technology change, led by AI, is both an opportunity for new managed services and a substitute for existing ones. Brazil tax matters of about USD 27 million remain unreserved and are small against the other factors.
### Strengths, weaknesses, opportunities and threats in credit terms

Strengths are the absence of any maturity before 2031, a high-margin installed-base franchise, contract backlog and a diversified client list, and the absence of owner-driven leakage. Weaknesses are fixed claims that absorb 94.23% of EBITDA, a digital workplace business with falling profit, earnings that depend on one fourth-quarter renewal season, and a pension obligation that competes for cash. Opportunities that could improve credit quality are the completion of the pension settlement programme in the first half of 2027, which should reduce required contributions, growth in ClearPath renewals and managed services for AI workloads, and cost savings from restructuring. Threats that could weaken it are AI-driven substitution of services, competitor pricing, a shift of ClearPath to subscription, and a single refinancing window in 2030 and 2031 at a time when the pension schedule is still heavy.

### Financial profile and credit quality

Across nine dimensions the profile is mostly average with weakness where cash is concerned. Scale and market position are average: revenue of USD 1,957.1 million over the last twelve months is modest against competitors that the company says have greater resources. Competitive advantage is average, strong in the ClearPath installed base and weak in digital workplace. Business diversification is average, with three segments, no client above 10% and 47.59% of FY2025 revenue earned outside the United States and the United Kingdom, but profit is concentrated. Cost and capex flexibility is average, since capital expenditure is 4.33% of revenue but overhead absorbs 79.34% of gross profit. Margin stability is weak, with EBITDA margin of 8.91% in FY2025 and 9.28% on the last twelve months, down from 10.15% in FY2024. Free cash flow stability is weak, with an outflow of USD 46.4 million. Ability to refinance and access capital markets is average, shown by the June 2025 refinancing but at a higher coupon and with ratings of B and B2. Liquidity position is average, with USD 353.3 million and no maturity before 2031. Financial policy and governance are average, with no sponsor, unqualified audit opinions and a debt-funded pension contribution. The main supports are the maturity profile and the ClearPath franchise; the main constraints are cash conversion and the pension; the trend is stable revenue with weaker cash, and the missing datapoints are covenant levels, the borrowing base and an issuer-defined EBITDA.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_uis-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 36; 10-K_2025-12-31_uis-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 143; calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C4; calculation C11
### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

Over the next 12 to 24 months earnings depend on the fourth-quarter 2026 renewal season, while cash depends on interest and pensions: the coupon is fixed at about USD 74.21 million a year and pension contributions are about USD 97 million in 2026 and about USD 101 million in 2027, so the cash gap stays negative on last-twelve-months earnings and liquidity funds it. Tailwinds are rising contract value, backlog above the prior year, an improving cloud segment margin of 22.48%, a joint venture margin benefit of about USD 12 million in 2026 and cost actions; headwinds are the ClearPath nine-month decline, falling digital workplace profit, AI substitution, competitor pricing and the loss of the joint venture benefit if the transaction does not recur. Over three to five years the pension settlement programme should lower obligations, contributions of about USD 241 million over 2028 to 2030 are lighter than 2026, and the decisive event is refinancing the ABL in June 2030 and the notes in January 2031, which is easier if EBITDA has recovered. Management gives no numeric revenue or earnings guidance in the filings, so this outlook is the analyst's reading of the disclosed schedules.

### Downside scenario

The scenario that matters is a further decline in ClearPath renewals and digital workplace profit, not a generic recession. The first operational break would be a weak fourth-quarter renewal season, because enterprise computing supplied an implied 74.75% of fourth-quarter 2025 segment gross profit. If the observed nine-month declines were repeated, with ClearPath revenue down 9.14% at the enterprise computing gross margin and digital workplace gross profit down 28.05%, EBITDA would fall by about USD 42.46 million to USD 139.24 million, total leverage would rise to 5.25x, cover would fall to 1.68x and the fixed-claims cash gap would widen to USD 116.77 million a year. Liquidity of USD 353.3 million would then last about 3.03 years, shorter than the 4.16 years to the notes' maturity, and a smaller receivables base would also reduce ABL availability and move it toward the USD 12.5 million level at which the fixed charge test applies. Management levers are capital expenditure, restructuring and the pension settlement schedule, but none of them closes a gap of that size without damaging the ClearPath and services base; resilience appears sufficient to avoid a liquidity crisis for about three years but not to refinance the notes from internal cash, and the ratio of the stress to the cushion is an illustration, not a forecast.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_uis-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 72–73; calculation C8; calculation C10; calculation C13; calculation C17
### Overall credit view

Overall, Unisys presents an adequate business profile supported by an installed-base software franchise, contract backlog and the absence of any maturity before 2031, but credit quality is constrained by fixed claims that absorb 94.23% of EBITDA (74.31% before a non-cash impairment), falling digital workplace profit and a heavy pension schedule. Cash-flow durability appears weak because free cash flow was an outflow of USD 46.4 million. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on EBITDA recovering before the 2030 and 2031 window, and on the fourth-quarter renewal season in between. The primary downside path is a weak ClearPath renewal season combined with continued digital workplace erosion, which raises leverage to 5.25x and uses liquidity before the notes mature. Further analysis would require the issuer's own EBITDA definition, covenant levels, the borrowing base, the US share of future pension contributions and the proxy statement. Top risk: fixed interest and pension claims that exceed earnings in a business whose profit depends on a single renewal season.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C6; calculation C7; calculation C17

### Strengths and weaknesses

Credit strengths are four. No debt matures before January 2031 except USD 13.3 million, and liquidity of USD 353.3 million would fund the current cash gap for about 4.75 years, which lowers near-term default risk. The ClearPath installed base earns 61.17% of segment gross profit and its renewal contract value rose 33% over nine months, which supports EBITDA and the case for refinancing. Backlog of USD 2.92 billion and the absence of any client above 10% of revenue limit revenue loss from a single event. No dividend has been paid since 1990 and no sponsor exists to extract cash, so owner leakage is not a risk.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_uis-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-K_2025-12-31_uis-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 60; calculation C8; calculation C13; calculation C15

Credit weaknesses are five. The coupon and 2026 pension contributions take 94.23% of EBITDA and free cash flow is negative, so liquidity is used each year. Pension contributions tie to the ABL maturity through the USD 100.0 million US contribution test. Digital workplace gross margin fell to 11.17% from 15.86% and its goodwill is gone, which removes a cushion and shows price pressure. Earnings are back-ended, with an implied 74.75% of fourth-quarter 2025 segment gross profit from enterprise computing, so one renewal season decides the year. Refinancing of the ABL and the notes falls within about 7 months in 2030 and 2031 at a coupon 3.75 percentage points above the notes it replaced.

## Gaps

- No filing states an adjusted or covenant EBITDA, so EBITDA is derived from operating income and depreciation and amortization, and no bridge to an issuer-defined measure exists. Severity medium. The company's own reconciliation, if it publishes one, would close it.

- The ABL borrowing base and the minimum fixed charge coverage level are not printed, so headroom to the facility test is not established beyond the USD 12.5 million availability level. Severity medium. The credit agreement and a compliance certificate would close it.

- Pension contribution estimates for 2027 onward are global, while the ABL springing maturity applies to US contributions only, so the nearest facility trigger cannot be dated. Severity medium. A US split of the 2027 estimate would close it.

- Agency ratings of B and B2 are stated as at the FY2025 annual report and no later agency commentary, peer set or market price is supplied, so market access and relative standing among leveraged IT services issuers are not established. Severity medium.

- No discrete fourth-quarter 2025 statements are printed, so the fourth-quarter shares of revenue and segment profit are derived by subtraction and the renewal-season dependence rests on that derivation. Severity low. A fourth-quarter release would close it.

- Restructuring savings, the timing of any shift of ClearPath to subscription and the nature of the first-quarter 2026 joint venture transaction are not quantified in the filings, so the outlook is the analyst's reading of disclosed schedules and management gives no numeric guidance. Severity low.

- Board composition, director independence, holder percentages and related-party dealings are not supplied, so governance conclusions beyond the audit committee are provisional. Severity low. The proxy statement would close it.
- Legal capacity, security ranking and recovery questions are outside this module and are not assessed here. Severity not applicable.
